title: Ops Micropanel: GPU Pool Burst Composer and Cost-Shift Preview
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design and prototype an inline ops micropanel embedded in the Dedicated Pools list that lets operators compose burst/autoscale intents and preview the projected cost and latency impact before applying them. The micropanel balances compactness for quick overrides with an expandable detail view for simulation. Key goals: 1) surface real-time health signals (utilization, tail latency, error rate), 2) allow quick burst sizing and hysteresis knobs, 3) show a simulated cost-shift chart for the next 24/72 hours based on recent traffic and a chosen burst policy, and 4) expose rollback / canary controls tied to rollout policy rules. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma frames for compact and expanded states, interactive prototype for usability testing, component spec for dev, and acceptance criteria for QA.
acceptance_criteria: Compact micropanel appears on each pool row and expands to detail view on click
Health strip shows utilization, p95 latency, KV cache hit %, and current queued requests with hover tooltips
Burst composer lets operator select duration, GPU burst percentage, and hysteresis threshold with inline validation
Cost-shift preview displays delta in estimated tokens/hour spend, projected 24h cost curve, and expected change to per-token latency
Apply action triggers a review modal summarizing potential user impact with a one-click quick-apply or scheduled apply option
Prototype includes failure path where burst cannot be scheduled and suggests fallback model variant
Design spec includes accessible color tokens, micro-interaction timings, and responsive states for narrow consoles
